positiveFlows.title: PROJECT TITLE:   FULL TITLE: NEXT-GENERATION MONITORING: SATELLITE REMOTE SENSING AND EDNA INTEGRATION FOR THE EARLY DETECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF AQUATIC INVASIVE PLANTS IN THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI BASINPROJECT PERIOD: 1 30 2025 THROUGH 1 29 2028  AWARD PURPOSE: EFFECTIVE TOOLS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR BETTER MONITORING AND MANAGING AQUATIC INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES IN THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER BASIN. AN INTEGRATIVE APPROACH COMBINING REMOTE SENSING AND ENVIRONMENTAL DNA (EDNA) OFFERS A COST- EFFECTIVE EARLY DETECTION AND MANAGEMENT SOLUTION. THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO DEVELOP REMOTE SENSING APPLICATIONS TO PINPOINT THE MOST LIKELY LOCATIONS AND TIMES FOR THE PRESENCE OF AQUATIC INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES, THEREBY STREAMLINING EDNA SAMPLE COLLECTION AND MAKING IT MORE EFFICIENT AND COST-EFFECTIVE. THIS INTEGRATIVE APPROACH WILL IDENTIFY AND MAP THREE AQUATIC INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES OF HIGH INTEREST TO THE RAPID ENVIRONMENTAL (E)DNA ASSESSMENT AND DEPLOYMENT INITIATIVE   NETWORK ORGANIZED BY THE U.S. GEOLOGICAL SURVEY. THEINTEGRATIVE METHODOLOGY WILL ALSO BE EXTENDED TO OTHER HIGH-PRIORITY INVASIVE SPECIES WITHIN THE BASIN, ENHANCING THE OVERALL EFFECTIVENESS OF MONITORING AND MANAGEMENT EFFORTS.  ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: THE RESEARCHERS WILL EMPLOY A MULTISCALE APPROACH, STARTING WITH EXPERIMENTAL WORK AT THE PLANT LEVEL AND EXPANDING TO CATCHMENT-SCALE SURVEYS, TO DEVELOP A REMOTE-SENSING-INFORMED EDNA PROTOCOL FOR EARLY DETECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF AQUATIC INVASIVE PLANTS. IN THE FIRST YEAR, A MESOCOSM EXPERIMENT WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INFORMATION ON HOW PLANT BIOMASS AND PHENOLOGY AFFECT EDNA DETECTION PROBABILITIES. THIS DATA WILL CALIBRATE A FIELD SURVEY TO ANALYZE THE AGREEMENT BETWEEN REMOTE SENSING AND EDNA DETECTION PROBABILITIES OVER A GROWING SEASON. ULTIMATELY, INSIGHTS FROM THESE SMALL-SCALE EXPERIMENTS WILL INFORM A COMPREHENSIVE MONITORING PROTOCOL AT THE CATCHMENT SCALE. TO EFFECTIVELY TRANSFER THE RESULTS TO STAKEHOLDERS AND RESEARCHERS, THE RESEARCHERS WILL ORGANIZE A WORKSHOP WITHIN THE USGS- SUPPORTED COMMUNITIES OF PRACTICE.  ADDITIONALLY, THE RESEARCHERS WILL COLLABORATE WITH UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SPECIALISTS TO CREATE PUBLICLY AVAILABLE FACT SHEETS, FACILITATING THE TRANSITION OF THE RESULTS INTO ACTIONABLE MANAGEMENT OUTCOMES. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: THIS RESEARCH PROJECT WILL BENEFIT RESOURCE MANAGERS AND BASIN STAKEHOLDERS BY PROVIDING AN INNOVATIVE AND INTEGRATIVE PROTOCOL FOR THE EARLY DETECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF AQUATIC INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES. IT WILL OFFER CRUCIAL INFORMATION ON SPECIES TARGETED BY THE RAPID ENVIRONMENTAL (E)DNA ASSESSMENT AND DEPLOYMENT INITIATIVE   NETWORK, IMPROVING THE ABILITY TO MONITOR AND CONTROL THESE INVASIVE SPECIES EFFECTIVELY. FOR EXAMPLE, DOM INFLUENCES THE TOXICITY OF HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS, THE PRODUCTION OF HARMFUL DISINFECTION BYPRODUCTS IN DRINKING WATER, AND THE PRODUCTION OF GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS ON REGIONAL AND GLOBAL SCALES. THE INFLUENCE OF DOM ON WATER RESOURCES DEPENDS ON ITS CONCENTRATION, WHICH VARIES SEASONALLY AND WITH STORMS. LOCAL TO REGIONAL SCALE IN SITU OBSERVATIONS HAVE DOCUMENTED CHANGES OVER TIME IN DOM CONCENTRATION POTENTIALLY DUE TO SHIFTS IN CLIMATE OR LAND-USE.HOWEVER, OBSERVATIONS OF DOM IN INLAND WATERS ACROSS MULTIPLE SCALES HAS LIMITED CAPACITY TO QUANTIFY OR PREDICT THE CHANGES IN DOM NEEDED TO INFORM THE MANAGEMENT OF THE NATIONS WATER RESOURCES.ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED:TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, PROPOSE TO PROVIDE REMOTE SENSING-DERIVED ESTIMATES OF DOM CONCENTRATION FOR SELECTED LAKES AND RIVERS ACROSS THE CONTINENTAL US FROM 1984-2024. NOTABLY, THIS WORK WILL BUILD UPON EXISTING EFFORTS AT THE U.S. GEOLOGICAL SURVEY NEXT GENERATION WATER OBSERVING SYSTEM WHERE MATCHED IN SITU DOM CONCENTRATIONS WILL BE PAIRED WITH SURFACE REFLECTANCE VALUES FROM LANDSAT 5, 7, 8, AND 9 AS WELL AS SENTINEL 2. WILL HIRE A POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER WHO WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR BUILDING PREDICTIVE MODELS BASED ON THE KNOWNOBSERVATIONS OF DOM IN LAKES AND RIVERS.DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES PRODUCTS WILL INCLUDE (1) A DATA RELEASE OF INTERNALLY CONSISTENT NATIONAL-SCALE DOM DATA, (2) PUBLICATION OF STATISTICAL AND MACHINE LEARNING MODELS PREDICTING DOM CONCENTRATIONS AT A NATIONAL SCALE, AND (3) AT LEAST ONE JOURNAL ARTICLE DOCUMENTING MODELS AND SYNTHESIZING RESULTS TO INFORM FUTURE WATER QUALITY OBSERVATION PROGRAMS AND WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE USGS WATER MONITORING PROGRAMS, WATER RESOURCE DECISION MAKERS, AND THE BROADER AQUATIC SCIENCE COMMUNITY.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES:A MAJOR MOTIVATION FOR THIS WORK IS THE PUBLICATION OF NOVEL DATASETS FOR EXPLORATION AND APPLICATION BY THE BROADER SCIENTIFIC AND WATER RESOURCE PRACTITIONER COMMUNITIES. THE DATASET WILL BE PUBLISHED IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL DATA INITIATIVE REPOSITORY, A USGS-APPROVED DATA PLATFORM. ALL CODING WORKFLOWS WILL BE MADE PUBLIC ON USGS GITLAB REPOSITORIES. NEXT GENERATION WATER OBSERVING SYSTEM LEADERSHIP AND PROGRAM DECISION MAKING WILL BE INFORMEDBY INTERIM PROJECT ACTIVITY SUMMARIES, PRESENTATIONS, AND THE FINAL PRODUCTS. ANTICIPATE THE RESULTS OF THIS PROJECT TO INFORM FUTURE NATIONAL SCALE WATER QUALITY MONITORING STRATEGIES. FINALLY, SINCE THE DATA WILL BE PUBLICLY AVAILABLE, THERE ARE MANY INTERESTING SCIENTIFIC QUESTIONS THAT CAN BE PROBED REGARDING THE SPATIOTEMPORAL VARIABILITY OF DISSOLVED ORGANIC CARBON IN US INLAND WATERS.SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIESTHE PI AT THE SUBRECIPIENT UNIVERSITY WILL SERVE AS A FACULTY MENTOR FOR THE POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER ON THIS PROJECT.

PROJECT PERIOD: 2 3 25-2 2 27PROJECT TITLE: MAPPING LOCAL SOIL MOISTURE WITH UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLE BASED L-BAND SENSORSOIL MOISTURE IS AN IMPORTANT VARIABLE IN THE TERRESTRIAL HYDROLOGICAL CYCLE. OBSERVATIONS ORMODELING OF SOIL MOISTURE AT HIGH SPATIAL RESOLUTION HAS PROVEN DIFFICULT DUE TO COMPLEXINTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE LAND SURFACE AND ATMOSPHERE THAT MAKE SOIL MOISTURE HIGHLY VARIABLE INTIME AND SPACE. IN TERMS OF IN-SITU OBSERVATIONS, MAINTAINING A HIGH SPATIAL DENSITY IS TIMECONSUMING AND EXPENSIVE. SATELLITE OBSERVATIONS ARE LIMITED BY A TRADEOFF BETWEEN SPATIALRESOLUTION AND TEMPORAL REVISITS, AND HIGH SPATIAL OBSERVATIONS CAN ONLY BE ACHIEVED IF THETEMPORAL REPEAT IS INFREQUENT.
